reviews.title: Pretty busy, and currently under renovations!
reviews.text: A beautiful building overlooking the Washington Monument and the Capitol Hill at the other end, and there was no more appropriate president to reside in that space other than the man who abolished slavery, Thomas Jefferson!During my visit, the left side of the memorial was under renovation, and so I was unable to take a nice picture of the memorial's exterior. The memorial itself was pretty iconic, seen in many tourist photos and it's pretty much self-explanatory. I like that he is looking straight to the monument and the capitol.

reviews.title: Lincoln Memorial
reviews.text: One of the great attractions of Washington D.C. - a fantastic building and a fantastic memorial for one of the great presidents of all time. A classic place that you can recognize from so many movies, news broadcasts, etc.

reviews.title: Iconic Memorial
reviews.text: The Lincoln Memorial is an iconic memorial on the National Mall dedicated to the 16th President of the United States. When I went, the memorial was unfortunately under construction which blocked off most of the stairs. Other than that, it was very surreal to visit and have great views of the Washington Monument and the rest of the National Mall.

reviews.title: The view!
reviews.text: I had some free time and decided to visit. There is a lot of walking. This is under renovation. The steps are getting worked on. The view! There were a lot of people. Must see.

reviews.title: Must see
reviews.text: Pictures do not compare to this magnificent memorial. Crowded, however people will let you get your pictures. Don’t miss this.

reviews.title: Fantastic
reviews.text: A must do for a trip to Washington. It's at the end of the national mall, so can be quite a walk. We visited it twice, once as part of a bike tour and the other as part of a night time bus trip. Awesome statue. We went on a Thursday morning and a Thursday night and it was quite busy both times, but it was worth it seeing it during the day and night.

reviews.title: President Lincoln Monument
reviews.text: Long walking the monument but so worth the time  love two options for getting to the top steps or ramp very helpful and kept the heavy foot traffic moving

reviews.title: A Majestic Tribute to an American Icon
reviews.text: The Lincoln Memorial in D.C. is awe-inspiring. The grand statue and famous speech inscriptions are deeply moving. Enjoy breathtaking views of the Reflecting Pool and Washington Monument, especially at sunset. A must-visit!

reviews.title: Excelent!
reviews.text: Very impressive, I have been there in 2014, then, after 10 years, I have returned to visit Lincoln Memorial. It is an amazing place, there is no doubt why there are lots of people visiting it. I'm sharing some pictures to try to express the feeling of being there.

reviews.title: 87 Steps from the reflecting pool - 4 Score + 7
reviews.text: Truly solemn and amazing. Even with many other visitors, the tone is hushed and reverent. I am glad I went alone, I was able to take all the time I wanted to read appreciate.

reviews.title: Huge size!

reviews.title: Favorite memorial
reviews.text: National treasure. Impressive memorial of a great American. Well-maintained and views from every direction give a different optical illusion.

reviews.title: Trip with two teenage boys in DC
reviews.text: My husband & I took our grandsons, 12 & 14 to DC so they could enjoy and experience our nation's capital. We had 3 full days and we really filled them. We stayed in the Capital Hill/Navy Yard area which does have many restaurants, is close to a Metro station as well as the Baeball stadium. For the Air & Space museum get tickets ahead - it gets full so ticket/passes are needed (free). we go to the Hirschorn Modern Art museum, The Potrait Museum, The Holocaust Museum, American History museum. Also had a tour of the White House as well as the Capital. The Capital tour was a big hit. Made it to most of the monuments during the day but also went back at night because they are stunning at night. Last museum was the International Spy Museum (not a mithsonian and $ticket needed. Went to the National Zoo too, although if short on time skip it. Eastern Market (Capital Hill) is a great stop too. We never made it to Georgetown - next time! (I've been there many times so I didn't mind)  Our boys were very engaged at all the Museums - thrye loved Spy Museum.

reviews.title: Guess it’s a must see
reviews.text: As a European I might be a bit allergic to bombastic architecture and person centered cults. While I deeply respect and appreciate this presidents efforts and achievements, I shy away from the efforts to turn this memorial into a place of worship. Fitting, though, it is built on stilts to make it appear elevated in the landscape. And even more interesting, they are now working on turning the vault under the structure into an exhibition area, including the graffiti left from the workers who built it.

reviews.title: Be careful during work
reviews.text: The best known memorial dating only from the 1930s. The view is magnificent all the way to the congress. Lots of people all the time. Work prevents you from going to the stairs.

reviews.title: Very busy!
reviews.text: A must see memorial, but it was very busy when we were there. Quite a few school groups too, so a little difficult to get good photos. Not a criticism, just something to be aware of

reviews.title: Go see Abe!
reviews.text: One of the coolest experiences.....and worth the time and effort to see....it is truly awe-inspiring to see in person.

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: The Lincoln Memorial is way bigger in real life than I thought it would be. The whole memorial is very, very cool. It's free of course and you can get some great photos with the statue and the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool. This is also a 15 minute walk away from the White House and Washington Memorial, which you should also check out. Overall, this is probably one of the most iconic spots in DC and therefore a must-see attraction.

reviews.title: Awesome place
reviews.text: Awesome place to go see the Lincoln memorial. Until you see the statue you don’t realise how big it is . Also from where Lincoln is facing , it’s almost like he’s watching the Washington monument and capitol building as they appear to be in a straight line. Don’t miss it you are there

reviews.title: Another Bucket List Site
reviews.text: I had eagerly looked forward to to the Lincoln Memorial, Pres. Lincoln being my most revered President. We were there around sunset, so the picture-taking wasn’t the best. There was a huge accessible ramp constructed to bypass construction taking place, and construction fencing and barriers blocked part of the view of the iconic memorial and statue from below. I walked up the stairs to the inside, though the lighting inside wasn’t great for my pictures at that time of day. I was somewhat dismayed at the numerous teenage students who were milling about, shouting and laughing, and taking selfies, showing no reverence or thought for where they were. Still, standing at the foot of the statue was an awe-inspiring experience to see & ponder. I’ve very glad I went there, and would recommend as a Must-See memorial in Washington DC.

reviews.title: Impressive
reviews.text: Free, historical, it's super interesting for any history fan.No need to wait long, and it's not complicated to have beautiful souvenir photos.

reviews.title: Impressive memorial
reviews.text: One of the many beautiful memorials in Washington DC. The view from there is wonderful over the National Mall to the Capitol. The size is very impressive. Seen so often in many films and then suddenly you are standing in front of it. The texts engraved on the wall are also worth reading.At the moment the memorial is only partially open because it is being built or renovated, like many places in Washington DC. The rush of visitors to the open site is therefore all the greater.

reviews.title: Rest
reviews.text: A very interesting place. I recommend everyone to go there.. it’s great for a walk with family or even alone...

reviews.title: A Great Memorial to a Great Man
reviews.text: I arrived at the Memorial early on a Tuesday morning before the tourist and school groups arrived, and for at least 15 minutes had the Memorial to myself.The Memorial is an impressive building based on Neo classical architecture and the sculpture of Lincoln is fantastic, The murals and inscription on the walls inside are also very impressive. There is some construction taking place outside of the memorial so this sails the exterior views of the front of the structure.There are also great views of the National Mall, Monument and Capitol Building from the Memorial. It can become very busy at peak times so visit early as I did.

reviews.title: Nice but under construction

reviews.title: The Lincoln Memorial

reviews.title: Night experience
reviews.text: Security was present, I enjoyed going at night but was scary not knowing how to find the metro station back or finding taxis around to take us to a subway station.

reviews.title: A historical monument well worth a visit
reviews.text: Mighty beautiful building. Lincoln sat safely watching over us. Beautiful view and not too many people. Well worth a visit

reviews.title: AMAZING
reviews.text: We were fortunate to go on a rainy, cloudy day, and there were not many other groups there.  We took our time, and read the speeches on both sides of the memorial.  POWERFUL!

reviews.title: Cool place to see, be mindful of crowds
reviews.text: It was busy! Currently under construction, have lots of patience with crowds but cool place to visit. Lines can be long to get up the museum.

reviews.title: Construction in progress
reviews.text: À wonderful memorial to our 16th President that everyone should visit when in DC. Currently in the middle of a 69 million dollar upgrade to the lower level which is scheduled to be completed by 2026. Due to the construction, restrooms are currently relocated nearby.

reviews.title: An icon of American history
reviews.text: The Lincoln Memorial solemnly commemorates President Abraham Lincoln, and its majestic columns and towering statue evoke dignified respect and contemplation, making it a must-see for anyone exploring Washington, D.C.

reviews.title: Lincoln memorial
reviews.text: The Lincoln memorial is undergoing renovations and construction of the Lincoln memorial museum which are supposed to be completed in 2026. Some of the views will be obstructed.

reviews.title: Stunning to see at night, but its busy
reviews.text: This was my first time visiting DC. I was visiting my son who was recovering from an injury during deployment.  We took advantage of this opportunity and explored DC. The number one thing I had to see was the Lincoln Memorial.  What an experience to see it up close. Stunning. Be prepared it's busy, very busy. Even at night around 8 pm.  It is huge and there are steps. They were working on a ramp for wheelchair,  but not completed as if March 2024. This is a must.

reviews.title: Monuments at night
reviews.text: Do not go see the Monuments at night! They are all very very dimly lit and are extremely difficult to see. Can hardly read any of the inscriptions and the details of the monuments are hidden in the dark.

reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.text: This is an amazing memorial. But it's crowded. Don't expect peace and quiet or alone time. This place is packed with people. It's still a must-see and an amazing place to go.

reviews.title: Timeless Majesty: The Lincoln Memorial Experience
reviews.text: The Lincoln Memorial is just awe-inspiring. Huge statue of Lincoln, beautiful setting with the Reflecting Pool. It's like stepping into history and feeling all patriotic. Must-see in D.C. for sure!

reviews.title: Impressive and Crowded
reviews.text: Took the crew for a day trip in DC over Christmas break.  Seeing the Lincoln Memorial was a must.  It is historical, impressive, and very crowded.  There was also a lot of work going on around it.  Regardless, it was a highlight of the trip for the kids.  Definitely worth checking out while in DC.  Just don't expect a quiet, sombre moment alone with Abe.  You will have people all around you.

reviews.title: History
reviews.text: This IS American history.  It is under construction but you can still get access to see it. Definitely a must see when in D.C.

reviews.title: Now that's a ststue!
reviews.text: A towering figure of American history deserves a towering statue, and the Lincoln Memorial fits the bill. But the memorial is more than just the statue. The building is itself impressive and the associated displays add depth to the tale behind the man. This is a definite DC must visit.

reviews.title: A Must See in Washington DC
reviews.text: We visited twice, once on our own in the day time and later, on a night time tour.  Both times it was crowded (though less so at night).  In the day time it was very crowded, and it is worth patiently navigating your way through the crowds to view this impressive monument up close and take in the speech inscribed in stone, and other information about the 16th President.  (A little useful tip: underneath, there are public toilets - not always easy to find in US cities).

reviews.title: Park Police are strict!
reviews.text: I have lived in Washington for 20 years, and used to work in very close proximity to this Monument for almost 15 of those. So I have been to this Monument many times, and sat on its steps to eat lunch and have gone during work hours just as a little break to sit back and awe at. Of course I have taken several guests there at night, and it's really beautiful and a magical place to be. I do recall hanging out at the monument with an ex-boyfriend and we had coffee with us. We attempted to sneak around to the back side and consume our hot beverages during the cold weather as it was raining. It really would have been a truly romantic evening and a much more memorable experience had the Park police not kicked us out for having food and drink, or rather drink on the premises. This was just coffee mind you and nothing illegal. We weren't doing anything else other than just wanting to have a private defensive place to sit and enjoy a record and the Magical atmosphere. So if you do go, I recommend you don't bring any hot beverages, or any food or beverage that would be consumed on the monument premises. It's a wonderful place to go and be pensive, but I think they want people to just come up see Mr Lincoln, take a few pictures and then go.

reviews.title: Wonderful memorial!
reviews.text: The Lincoln Memorial has always been my favorite memorial in D.C. and it's likely because Lincoln is one of my favorite presidents. It's a stunning tribute to him and it's a very thought-provoking place to be, even when it's absolutely crowded. The architecture of the building itself is gorgeous and that is only enhanced by the statue of Lincoln himself. My favorite way of seeing this is it lit up at night and the memory of that is one that I will keep with me forever. It's a beautiful memorial and one you should make sure to see once in your life.

reviews.title: Impressive city, a lot of history.
reviews.text: A city with a lot of history, I loved the museums and I think it's great that entry to them, for the most part, is free.

reviews.title: Where History Rocks and Abe Rules!
reviews.text: The Lincoln Memorial is like a history hug! With its grand marble vibes and Honest Abe statue, it's like stepping into a patriotic daydream. The words on the walls give you serious inspo, and the chill by the reflective pool is perfect for deep thoughts or a picnic. It's basically a giant reminder that history can be cool, and hey, Abe was a legend!

reviews.title: Lincoln Memorial
reviews.text: Definitely worth the visit if you are in DC area. You can feel all the history and important events/speeches that have taken place here just by walking up the steep steps to go up to Abe directly

reviews.title: Got to see the great man!
reviews.text: The Memorial was/is undergoing some work when we visited. This greatly restricted access and the steps were dangerously crowded.  The shop must be the smallest gift shop in the US!!  Didn't detract from the experience though.

reviews.title: A must-do
reviews.text: Always worth a visit when in DC. There’s construction underway so half the stairway leading up to the memorial is closed. This means that the place where Martin Luther King Jr gave his legendary speech is not currently able to be seen. I sincerely hope that when the construction is complete, that location is given the focus it deserves as previously it was lost.

reviews.title: Amazing place

reviews.title: Lincoln Memorial: Timeless Reflections
reviews.text: The Lincoln Memorial is a powerful symbol of American history in the heart of Washington, D.C. The imposing statue of Abraham Lincoln and the serene Reflecting Pool create a solemn yet awe-inspiring atmosphere. It's a must-visit, offering a brief but impactful glimpse into the nation's values and leadership.

reviews.title: Eternal Tribute
reviews.text: The Lincoln Memorial is a symbol of unity and equality. His majestic presence and iconic recorded speech inspire a sense of leadership and justice.

reviews.title: Beautiful Memorial
reviews.text: It is a monumental Memorial with a large Statue in honor of President Lincoln.All in high standard stones. To get to the Statue I took a walk through the park.

reviews.title: Truly spectacular
reviews.text: It is one of the most spectacular monuments we have ever seen. As the name suggests it is devoted to the 16th president of the USA, Abraham Lincoln. Abraham Lincoln  was assassinated on April 14, 1865 and two years later Congress incorporated the Lincoln Monument Association to build a memorial.  The Lincoln Memorial stands on the National Mall. From the Lincoln Memorial you can have a wonderful view on the Washington Memorial and the reflecting pools.I would recommend visiting it in the evening, too. It looks really spectacular. All memorials in Washington are free of costs.

reviews.title: Awe Inspiring
reviews.text: Even for us Canucks, this edifice is not just impressive in size, but meaning for the histories of both our countries.  After absorbing the magnificent statue we’ve seen in many films, take the time to reread the Gettysburg Address on the left of this simple space, and Lincoln’s second inaugural address on the right.  Then step down the stairs in front to where Martin Luther King gave his “I have a dream speech,” and enjoy this vista over reflecting pond down the Washington Monument.

reviews.title: Exuberant
reviews.text: It is worth visiting the center of thought in the United States!There one realizes the magnificence of the empire...

reviews.title: VERY GOOD

reviews.title: Huge
reviews.text: A must see in Washington, one of the coolest statues and monuments you'll ever see. Big and stately. Really a clear picture of how popular Abraham Lincoln is where he sits Richard looks out over Washington.

reviews.title: Impressive both inside and out
reviews.text: We went here in the evening. Very impressive and I never knew that the statue is 5m80. And then it stands on a pedestal. You have to climb to enter. The outside is covered in scaffolding, but luckily you don't notice it inside.

reviews.title: Well worth visiting
reviews.text: The memorial is nice, you'll need to take some steps to get to it. The statue is very big, there is information about him and the history on the wall.You can see the Washington monument from here through refection pool. I visited here on a Tuesday afternoon, it wasn't crowed.

reviews.title: Amazing Memorial to visit!
reviews.text: My husband and I are big Lincoln fans so I knew he needed to see this memorial. I myself have seen this when I was much younger so now that I'm a bit older it was great to experience it again! Unfortunetly, the memorial was under construction so that was a bit disappointed but the statue and main area where Lincole sits was not. It wasn't too busy and it was fun to see people dancing on the stairs leading up to the memorial. Its such a great likeness of him with all of this famous quotes around him. They do have a little gift shop there but there is also another one with more things just a bit aways away which is where we found what we were looking for. This is a must see in DC!

reviews.title: Impressive.

reviews.title: Monumental
reviews.text: The monument is one of a kind. It's enormous and conveys an important message. It is very accessible for people with disabilities as it has an elevator.

reviews.title: Our Visit at Night was INCREDIBLE
reviews.text: We went around 7 p.m. and it was the best part of our trip to DC.  We could see the Washington Monument and The Capitol from the Lincoln Memorial.  It was beautiful.  We spent some time near the statute of President Lincoln.

reviews.title: Lincoln
reviews.text: The day we visited it was pretty busy unlike the year before. Lincoln Memorial is now under construction and parts are fenced off. Still we’re able to get up to the monument, but very crowded and pictures were not as good.

reviews.title: Larger than life but under reconstruction
reviews.text: One of the few places I have seen litter ! Toilets ( sorry restrooms) were horrible . The monument is currently being renovated but you can still go in and see the statue .

reviews.title: Majesty

reviews.title: Iconic
reviews.text: Iconic in every way, walk up those steps and have that dream. The view down to the Monument and across  are something to remember.

reviews.title: Heaving but nice monument

There was some work going on so some of the steps were cordoned off but it looked tatty - they could have been more sympathetic in how they are keeping it whilst the work is being done. It was heaving too, on the steps and inside.

reviews.title: In Awe

So sadly I could not stand where Martin Luther king Jr stood when he delivered his iconic speech. However, it is still incredibly impressive to see and I have to say Americans know how to do a memorial as there are many other memorials in the vicinity that are also worth admiring. Definitely not to be missed if you’re in DC, I’d love to be able to live local and walk around the mall and the memorials whenever I pleased!

reviews.title: Well worth the visit.
reviews.text: It's exactly what you'd expect... very impressive.Some renovation work being done when we were there but, hey, it has to be done some time and nothing is inaccessible.

reviews.title: Great memorial
reviews.text: An absolute must! Very beautiful memorial in honor of the 16th President of the USA. Admission is free, but on a Saturday the number of visitors was very high.

reviews.title: Magnificent memory of Lincoln
reviews.text: A magnificence statue and memorial in the memory of a revolutionary man. As you as you step into the memorial, you can just feel how special this place is - and the importance he played in the history of the USA. A must see in Washington.

reviews.title: Four score and seven years ago… I only read it in a book and then I saw in real life…
reviews.text: Massive statue of one of America’s greatest public figure.  Good for those who can walk by steps but I didn’t see if there’s a ramp or elevator for elderlies and impaired. When we visited the front was under construction so you can’t really tKe a nice memorable pic of the whole building having said that still a good to see this tourist spot..

reviews.title: In the heart of the country
reviews.text: It takes a good day to be able to do the long walk that starts from the Lincoln statue and ends at the White House.The experience is excellent, the statue imposing and the surrounding area open and well maintained. Access is free.Next door there is a cafe and a gift shop with souvenirs that you will not find in the rest of the country. Recommended.

reviews.title: One of Washington's most famous monuments, imposing on the outside, evocative on the inside
reviews.text: The exterior of the building is splendid, characterized by a large staircase from which you can admire a wonderful view of The Mall up to the Washington Monument. Surrounded by a park where there are also refreshment points, and continuously connected to the rest of The Mall by the Bus Circulator, inside you can admire the very famous statue of Abraham Lincoln, enormous, surrounded by a series of columns that make it from frame. Very suggestive.

reviews.title: Very Educational
reviews.text: Visited Abraham Lincoln memorial, it is a museum, and very educational for those who are interested in understanding the history of the United States. There is a big statue of Abraham Lincoln and the important messages written on the wall.

reviews.title: It's a classic. 'Nuff said.
reviews.text: The first time I came to Washington DC, I missed this entirely. Not that I didn't know what it was (I've seen the Tim Burton Planet of the Apes, after all), but that I just never got the chance to see it. I've now been to DC four times, and I made sure to see it one the latter two. And as a history enthusiast, let me tell you: this is worth seeing in D.C. Is it a tourist trap? Oh, absolutely. It's crowded with schools and other visitors day and night, and it's genuinely time-consuming to get there and back via walking (unless you're looking for a lengthy walk, which you might be). But it's worth it for sure. Say what you want about glorifying the founding fathers of any country, but you FEEL the glory standing in front of this statue. You have to wonder if Honest Abe would like this monument, and I imagine he wouldn't really be a big fan of it personally. But his accomplishments certainly warrant his commemoration, and this is a more-than-worthy way to do so. It's a must-see attraction if you're in the city, that's for sure.Now I just need to get to the MLK monument, dammit...

reviews.title: A wonderful and fitting memorial honoring Abraham Lincoln
reviews.text: The Lincoln Memorial in Washington, D.C. is located at the western end of the National Mall at the opposite end of a long grass strip from the Capitol building. Visiting the Lincoln Memorial can be challenging if you are driving since finding parking can be a challenge due to its central location. I recommended utilizing public transportation or parking at nearby garages and lots, such as the Union Station Parking Garage or the Ronald Reagan Building and International Trade Center Parking Garage. You could also take a guided tour or utilize ride-sharing services. I rented a car and toured several sites that eveningThe main entrance to the monument is by broad steps on the eastern entrance. As you approach the memorial, the grandeur of the structure becomes increasingly apparent. The iconic 19-foot seated statue of President Lincoln commands the attention of all who visit. The larger-than-life figure exudes a sense of strength and wisdom, while the inscription of his immortal Gettysburg Address and Second Inaugural Address reminds us of his profound impact on the nation.The memorial's interior is a large chamber, adorned with murals depicting significant moments from Lincoln's life. The marble walls and wide spaces create an atmosphere of reverence and reflection. From the steps of the memorial, visitors are treated to panoramic views of the Reflecting Pool, the Washington Monument, and the U.S. Capitol, forming a breathtaking vista that encapsulates the spirit of the nation. It is not only a tribute to a remarkable leader but also serves as a gathering place for historic events and peaceful demonstrations. Its significance in American history and its architectural grandeur make it a must-visit destination for locals and tourists alike. The lighting on the steps at night is very limited so step carefully. If you were only going to see one monument in DC, I would choose this one.

reviews.title: Crowded but must-see
reviews.text: The Lincoln Memorial is a monument in Washington DC dedicated to Abraham Lincoln, the 16th President of the United States. It is located on the National Mall and is one of the most popular tourist destinations in the city.When there are a lot of people at the Lincoln Memorial, it can be a bit crowded and hectic. Visitors may have to navigate through crowds and lines to get inside the monument, especially during peak tourist season.Despite the crowds, the Lincoln Memorial is still a must-see destination. The monument is an impressive structure with 36 white marble columns and a large statue of Abraham Lincoln inside. The walls are inscribed with some of Lincoln's most famous speeches, including the Gettysburg Address and his Second Inaugural Address.Visitors may need to be patient and wait their turn to get a good view of the monument or to take a photo. However, the crowds also add to the energy and excitement of the experience.One tip for dealing with the crowds is to visit the monument early in the morning or later in the evening, when there are fewer people around. This can also provide a more peaceful and serene experience, and allow visitors to take in the beauty and grandeur of the monument without the distractions of large crowds.Overall, the Lincoln Memorial is a must-see destination for anyone visiting Washington DC, and despite the crowds, it's worth the effort to visit and pay tribute to one of the most important figures in American history.

reviews.title: From the Land of Lincoln to The Lincoln Monument
reviews.text: Always an amazing experience in Washington DC. My nephew got married in DC in Feb 2022 and had amazing Wedding Photos taken on the mall. The Lincoln Memorial is always special since we are from Illinois “the land of Lincoln”It’s a popular sight-seeing area so expect crowds but more important - EXPECT TO BEIN AWE! We’ve visited 4 times in the last 10 years and it never disappoints. It’s a great experience for families with school-aged children but it’s a place where people of all ages go to experience a piece of history.

reviews.title: So very impressive
reviews.text: The Lincoln Memorial is so very impressive...more than I had anticipated from pictures and movies. My first viewing was at night, under the lights, very few people.  It was a soft glow in the distance then a huge presence when up close.  A few details may be missed when visiting at night but I preferred that experience to the daylight, crowds and traffic.  Either time, its a place you want to visit and read Lincoln 's speeches. tiny gift store offered a lot of information.   Restrooms available.

reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.text: Amazing place to visit and to take in the true size of the memorial.  Great place to take pictures with amazing views from all sides.  It far exceeds any expectations from what you see in pictures.

reviews.title: Beautiful Building
reviews.text: Such an iconic building, it has to be visited and take in the scale of Lincoln's statue, along with the surrounding area of the Mall with all it's iconic museums and buildings

reviews.title: Awesome statue of Lincoln
reviews.text: The feeling is one of grandeur. Lincoln sitting on a pedestal. One can walk to it as one walks around the idal Basin. the steps leading into the Memorial is a good place to take photographs.

reviews.title: US history at crossroads
reviews.text: Abraham Lincoln is one of the most influential presidents of all time. The Lincoln Memorial is unsurprisingly the number one attraction in Washington DC. A temple-like structure reminiscent of Parthenon, it includes a huge Lincoln statue as well as his famous quotes. The view of the National Mall atop the stairs is particularly remarkable. Do come around sunset.

reviews.title: Worth The Journey
reviews.text: One of many must see sites when you visit our nations capitol. Museum in the basement with tablets inscribed with words of inspiration from Lincoln's multiple speeches. Also great views of our nations capitol.

reviews.title: Awesome sight!
reviews.text: Very imposing monument.  The statue hall is impressive. view to Washington monument is incredible at night!

reviews.title: Must see
reviews.text: Pretty cool memorial honoring a great president and fellow Illinoisian. The surrounding scenery and view are what picture postcards are made of.  Well worth the trip.

reviews.title: Washington's most beloved monument?
reviews.text: Although the Washington memorial is likely DCs most iconic monument, I would argue that the Lincoln memorial is the capital's most loved landmark. The majestic statue of Lincoln has been visited by millions of visitors over the years, who have been able to read an inscription of the Gettysburg address on one side of the statue, and an inscription of Lincoln's second inaugural address on the other side.Meanwhile, if you go below the monument, you will find a small Lincoln museum that contains quotes from arguably the most important president in US history. I am glad I came to this site and would recommend any fellow visitor to Washington to come here.

reviews.title: Freedom!
reviews.text: Just amazing, this is why I am proud to be a American and have the many freedoms we do!This was very emotional and highly recommend for all ages!

reviews.title: an architectural masterpiece
reviews.text: we visited it in the evening. I would recommend that you should also do it during the daytime. From there you can see the Washington Monument and you're also very close to the Vietnam Memorial plus some other sights. The Lincoln Statue is impressive and grand

reviews.title: Must see site to visit in DC
reviews.text: One of the top places to visit in DC.  Great views of the mall and Capitol, especially on a sunny day

reviews.title: Must visit, it's free
reviews.text: Incredibly big Lincoln Monument. You will find a lot of history written on the walls inside the memorial so go with time if you like history. It is worth a visit. Aside of the memorial it self, you get a great view of the park from the top of the stairs for really nice pictures. A must visit if you have time in DC. Won't regret it. It's free.

reviews.title: Iconic
reviews.text: Stop by when walking the mall.  Pick a sunny day.  Take the metro or take your chances finding parking.

reviews.title: Sightseeing tour
reviews.text: Fascinating monument, of a nations leader. Exhibit below is worth the visit.  Access for wheelchairs and toilets for everyone.

reviews.title: Another great place
reviews.text: Well, another great place for you to visit while in Washington D.CFrom here you can take a walk to some of the very famous attractions.

reviews.title: Lincoln Memorial is well worth the trip
reviews.text: Absolutely beautiful. Made chills run down my spine. What a tribute to our nations history. And we stayed until dark. The ambiance was amazing.

reviews.title: Great experience better to see in person recommend to wear comfortable sneakers lots of steps to get to the monument 🥰
reviews.text: Very impressive monument didn’t imagine how big the monument is in person and is also a beautiful view from there back 🥰🤗

reviews.title: Old Soldiers Never Die...
reviews.text: Time to revisit this photo we look in December 2013 of what looks like the ghost of a soldier walking behind our 3 granddaughters (gray figure). We had just been to the WW2 Memorial, and the figure looks like it is wearing a helmet and flack jacket. Photos taken by other members of our family at the same time show no one in gray behind or around them. Just an old soldier passing by, we guessed.

reviews.title: Must see memorial with view along the mall
reviews.text: This is one of the must see sights in Washington, it can be quite a serene place to enjoy the view of the mall and take in some history if you can shut out the crowds.

reviews.title: Historical Experience
reviews.text: We visited several times during our recent trip to WA/DC and loved it every time.  It's 100 years old now and carries all of the experiences people have had there from protests to celebrations.

reviews.title: Love this Memorial
reviews.text: This Memorial is great.  No trip is complete without a trip to see Abraham Lincoln.  It is amazing how much detail is in the monument.  I highly recommend seeing this one in the daylight as well as at night.

reviews.title: Best at Night
reviews.text: Amazing monument so much better to be seen at night as quite crowded during the day. Plus it is far more focussed at night with the lights, very powerful

reviews.title: Massive monument with interesting inscriptions on the walls
reviews.text: Definitely worth a walk out of town for this moment on a grand scale. Nice views across the Potomac to the rear of the monument

reviews.title: Do it by bike - save your feet!
reviews.text: Do it by bike as part of a trip around all the monuments - all at your own pace and without getting footsore and weary. Early morning before the crowds so that you get the vibe with Lincoln sitting above you, and then return for floodlight at night. They're very different and magical experiences.

reviews.title: Always a great stop

This is a great picture spot for the reflecting pool as well as the Lincoln Memorial itself.

reviews.title: MUST SEE

reviews.title: Great

reviews.title: Great, but needs work!
reviews.text: As this was at state capital, I would’ve wish to have seen it more clean and kept up with. On top of that, the people there were a tad bit disrespectful to the monument which was also disheartening. Overall, it was a nice visit, but there needs to be better keep up of the place. reviews.title: A Must-See on the Washington Mall
reviews.text: We visited in Fall season, and if you have the chance I'd suggest you do the same, as this can  be a very busy area of the Washington Mall.  The Lincoln Memorial is at the far west end of the Mall, and if you're like us, you'll find yourself walking from one end to the other making as many stops as your time allows.  If you visit the Washington DC Metro website, you'll be able to see that the train and bus lines make stop/s along the Mall.  I remember the 1st time we were in DC about 10 years ago, We bought what was I think a multi-day pass, used the heck out of it, and our car didn't leave our hotel the whole time we were there!But, back the the Lincoln Memorial.  It wasn't as crowded, as I stated the BUSY tourist season was over.  Such a beautiful building.   If you're able, take the time to walk around like we did, and take in the different views of the city at every turn.  Also, don't forget a good pair of shoes and have you phone charged, as you'll be taking SO many photos.

reviews.title: So much history in one place
reviews.text: This trip was my chance to show my 8 year old daughter the memorials and this was her favorite.  We were able to ride up on an electric scooter, find some parking areas on the edge, and walk up.  It was the same monument and yet different.  Took her to stand on the spot of Martin Luther King Jr.'s "I have a dream" speech.  You look out towards the Washington monument across the reflection pool and you can think about all of the other people that have been there and stood where you are.  There is just nothing like it.

reviews.title: Missed out
reviews.text: Went to DC recently to see a bit of history. Well a bit is all we saw. Travel through DC is a challenge to say the least. No one there seems to be tolerant of any type of traffic, so if you slow down to be sure you're turning on the right street because you're from out of town, or you slow up just to look at a site, you are honked at, yelled at, and given the finger. Lovely welcome for tourists - thanks!So after two days of fighting traffic and rude people, we cut our vacation two days short and decided if we were going to get to see any of the monuments or sites, we'd have to leave the hotel to get on the road before daybreak so no one would get mad because we were holding up traffic.We left our hotel at 4:00 A. Knowing nothing would be open to tour, we still wanted to get pictures of the more popular sites, such as the Lincoln Memorial. Imagine our disappointment when we found out you can get pictures of every side of the monument from the road/car EXCEPT the side old Abe is actually sitting on. Unfortunately, I am not able to walk a great distance, so even in the regular business hours, I wouldn't have been able to walk up any steps, but I had hoped to at least view the memorial from the car and get pictures. Nope, not able to do so. Not that we could see, anyway, but it's hard to see everything in the dark.Not to mention, with all the security around DC in general (which obviously is a good thing) you don't really push to try to get in somewhere that looks inaccessible as you don't know for sure if it looks that way by accident or on purpose, because you won't want to end up in custody for fear of them thinking your there to do some dastardly deed.The sheer size of the building is amazing and breathtaking, but I sure do wish we had gotten to see Lincoln.

reviews.title: Everyone who cares about US history has to stop here.

reviews.title: Immense
reviews.text: Wow.Seeing the memorial up close was memorable. The memorial is immense. From all angles, the view is spectacular. Reminds us all why Abe Lincoln is still among the favorite presidents ever celebrated.

reviews.title: Very impressive
reviews.text: A long hot day in August walking around the National mall, Gwen you finally climb all the steps the monument is ver impressive.

reviews.title: A must.. to see in person

Its grand during the day but its spectacular at night.   Lots of parking at this end of the mall, but the walk from Washington monument to the Lincoln Memorial is something else.. its long but well worth it.. the size and scale of this memorial leaves you speechless.  The history, the significance, and the stature of this memorial is a must see in person and stand at the feet of Lincoln Statue

reviews.title: Washington DC memorials

You would have thought I would have taken more pictures, but my emotions got the best of me. It was extremely crowded, everyone seemed to be drawn by the history. It was truly larger than life and a day I won’t ever forget.

reviews.title: A Must See

reviews.title: Iconic Memorial, great visit
reviews.text: Always wanted to see the Lincoln Memorial as it's an iconic site. A must see when visiting Washington DC. There were a lot of tourists and at times it was hard to obtain a clear photo but it's worth the walk from our hotel. Visited in July and the weather was very warm but the memorial is surrounded by trees and shade. It was a lovely experience.

reviews.title: Lincoln Memorial-Free Entry, Stunning at Night.
reviews.text: The Lincoln Memorial is one of the top destinations in DC. Entry is free, and we decided to visit at night when the air was cooler and there was a bit of a breeze.The statue of Abraham Lincoln is much larger than it seems in photos, and the side walls are engraved with two of Lincoln’s speeches.  It is a place filled with honor and thoughtful reflection. Also, make a point to stop near the top steps to find the marked location where Martin Luther King Jr. delivered the historic “I Have A Dream Speech”.

reviews.title: One of my favorite monuments in DC
reviews.text: The Lincoln Memorial is one of my favorites! I definitely suggest going earlier in the morning, as sometimes you may be the only one there, which is really nice when trying to take a pic.

reviews.title: Awe-inspiring, America at its best.
reviews.text: The Lincoln Memorial makes one think what America is at its best.  A time to reflect on the past, present, and future.  The grounds surrounding the Memorial are beautiful.  A definite site to see when visiting Washington, DC.

reviews.title: Get your pic and go
reviews.text: It's really crowded, even at dusk. The gift shop is really small - basically a closet. Go ad get your iconic picture, but don't spend a lot of time here.

reviews.title: Always a fun stop
reviews.text: It was crowded with college groups when we went, but still a good place to visit. Lots of stairs. Not too far from the parking at the Tidal Basin.

reviews.title: A must see!
reviews.text: Going there is mandatory if you’re in DC. I had never been there at night, and even when it was crowded it was wonderful to see the lights. I prefer visiting early in the morning, when there is just a few people.

reviews.title: Iconic and perfectly placed
reviews.text: We walked here on our first full day in the city.  It's sited at one end of the mall, which is the focal point fo the city, and opposite the Capitol Building situated at the far end.  The memorial is breathtaking with Lincoln sitting prominent and powerful in the centre, looking out towards the Washington memorial in the centre.  You have to climb some steps to get up to the monument and, with Lincoln facing you, there is an engraving in stone on the wall on the right with his second presidential address and his Gettysburg address on the wall on the right.  There are lots of people selling water and Ice Creams outside.  There are restrooms at the base of the monument on the left as you look upwards.  However, due to the significant amount of use they get, they appear not very well maintained.  As a monument it is fitting to a man of great standing and an absolute must for anyone visiting the Mall.   We also visited at night when we did an evening bus tour.  The photo's accompanying this show the different vista's.

reviews.title: Not to be missed!
reviews.text: Perfect for photos of the Washington Monument at the other end of the mall. There are two souvenier/refreshment shops nearby, one at the roadside and another down the steps near the side of the monument.

reviews.title: An iconic site

reviews.title: One of the absolute greatest monument buildings in the entire (history of the) world
reviews.text: PROS* Stand in awe at one of the world's most iconic famous and meaningful structures* Fantastic structure- an architectural marvel* Tremendous statue in thoughtful pensive pose- gigantic* A monument to our guiding principles and future as a nation* It feels like a temple or a shrine* A historical place to remember the events here through the ages* Unparalleled and unequaled views in both directions- the National Mall and towards Arlington National Cemetery* Learn about Lincoln from his speeches engraved on the walls and from the information downstairs* Free and unfettered access 24 hours a day* Celebrate its 100th anniversary in 2022* Bond with our nation's past and commit for a better future* Best later at night or early at dawn in the morningCONS* It can be always crowded* Tour groups (especially school groups) can be rowdy and disrespectful* Tour group guides speeches disturb the solitude that is an essential part of this shrine* Motorized and pedal bicycles roam freely at the base- dangerous* Truly inadequate lighting at night- dark! (see my many photos)- a danger for the visually- challenged"I VISITED THIS PLACE"...... as the first and most important stop on my nightime monuments tour for my family (we visited the adjacent Vietnam. Korea and MLK but did not get any further that night).  As stated and as seen in my many photos, the place after 2030/2100 was very crowded with noisy groups and it is quick dark and could be downright dangerous to thos who are disabled- and that was at night!!  Maybe everyone is learning of the secret to come at night, as I've posted on the TripAdvisor D.C. forum for years.So we returned at 0700 the next day and there were still plenty of people there, but it was much more managable, yet certainly not quiet nor solemn.  We walked around the entire perimeter of the building, at the level of the statue.This place deserves more than five starsTIPI've always said and written to go at night; now I add go at dawn PLEASE see my many photos- from night and from day and then from various lookouts, perches and observation points and backgrounds.  If you like this review and/or the many photos that will be attached, please click "helpful."

reviews.title: Such a great place

reviews.title: Who doesn’t love Lincoln?
reviews.text: Pros:CleanHistoricalSeemed safe, lots of cameras everywhere Could get very close to itYou were even able to ride scooters/bikes/etc around it! Cons:Like every monument in DC, this place was extremely crowded. Like, really super crowded. Good experience. I definitely recommend.

reviews.title: Don’t Miss It!
reviews.text: Amazing place that makes you proud to be an American. The history behind the memorial is very interesting.

reviews.title: Outstanding, educational and those stunning views
reviews.text: 21st May and the 4th stop on our tour of the National Mall. I didnt grasp the size of this memorial until we were actually there, the entire monument is huge, from the steps leading up (turn around for that magical view of the Washington Monument across the Reflecting pool), the statue of Lincoln himself to the enormous tablets of his famous speeches adorning the interior walls. reviews.title: You can't appreciate its grandeur unless you've been there
reviews.text: How many motion pictures have you seen that featured the Lincoln Memorial? From Jimmy Stewart to Tom Cruise to Clint Eastwood? You simply can't appreciate the grandeur of the place unless you've been there. It is a very humbling experience. Located at the west end of the National Mall in Washington, D.C., it was built to honor Abraham Lincoln, the 16th president of the United States. Construction began in 1914 and completed in 1922. On of the city's major tourist attractions -- it drew 7.8 million visitors in 2019 -- it is open 24 hours a day and has been the site of many famous speeches, including Martin Luther King Jr.'s  "I have a dream" speech o August 28, 1963. The structure echoes a neoclassical Greek temple, features Yule marble quarried in Colorado and measures 189.7 by 118.5 feet and is 99 feet tall. It is surrounded by a peristyle of 36 fluted Doric columns, one for each of the 36 states in the union at the time of Lincoln's death in 1865, and two columns at the  entrance behind the colonnade. The columns stand 44 feet tall with a base diameter of 7.5 feet. Leading up to the shrine on the east side are the main steps, which begin at the edge of the Reflecting Pool. There are three chambers in the memorial's interior divided by two rows of Ionic columns each 50 feet tall and 5.5 feet across at the base. The central chamber, which houses the famous 19-foot-tall seated sculpture of Lincoln, is 60 feet wide, 74 feet deep and 60 feet high. On the walls are inscriptions of two well-known speeches by Lincoln, the Gettysburg Address and his second inaugural address. The memorial was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1966.

reviews.title: As Lincoln said For the People!
reviews.text: The Lincoln Memorial is a US national memorial built to honor the 16th President of the United States, Abraham Lincoln. It is located on the western end of the National Mall in Washington, D.C., across from the Washington Monument. Taking the form of a neoclassical temple, the memorial's architect was Henry Bacon. The designer of the memorial interior's large central statue – Abraham Lincoln, 1920 – was Daniel Chester French; the Lincoln statue was carved by the Piccirilli Brothers.[3] The painter of the interior murals was Jules Guerin. Dedicated in May 1922, it is one of several memorials built to honor an American president. It has always been a major tourist attraction and since the 1930s has been a symbolic center focused on race relations. The history of this glorious building is more than incredible as the man who is depicted within it. Lincoln was a man of many attitudes feelings and ideals who was fought almost all the time. During the Civil War he had to actually fire a very famous General who was a friend of his. His name was McClellan, for some reason this general couldn't figure out when to fight!Lincoln it is said actually visited him and fired him replacing him with a big mouth cigar chewing General Named Grant! Well Grant got it done alright. We all know what happened to Grant now don't we?The building is in the form of a Greek Doric temple and contains a large seated sculpture of Abraham Lincoln and inscriptions of two well-known speeches by Lincoln, The Gettysburg Address and his second inaugural address. The memorial has been the site of many famous speeches, including Martin Luther King Jr.'s "I Have a Dream" speech, delivered on August 28, 1963, during the rally at the end of the March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom.Like other monuments on the National Mall – including the nearby Vietnam Veterans Memorial, Korean War Veterans Memorial, and National World War II Memorial – the memorial is administered by the National Park Service under its National Mall and Memorial Parks group. It has been listed on the National Register of Historic Places since October 15, 1966, and was ranked seventh on the American Institute of Architects 2007 list of America's Favorite Architecture. Once you are here though, you literally can spend the whole day walking the loop, that is the national mall, to end your day here.

reviews.title: Finally got to see this memorial
reviews.text: This statue is humongous! Seeing this on tv does not do it justice, this is so amazing that i actually climbed all the stairs to get a closer look. Again, this is all free to the public, no need to pay for something that's out there for anyone to see at anytime.

reviews.title: Spectacular
reviews.text: This monument is a must visit. Movies, documentaries, videos and pictures do not do it justice. It is a truly astonishing piece of work, a gigantic marble sculpture that you will never forget. It was fairly crowded when I attended but most people were respectful enough to move to allow for a proper picture and view of the sculpture.

reviews.title: THE iconic Memorial in DC
reviews.text: One of the first, and still one of the best. WOW. Has stood the test of time and still an amazing testament to an amazing man and President

reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.text: Photos do not do this memorial justice. It is a must see when visiting D.C.. It is located around the WW2, Korean War, and Vietnam Veterans Memorial. So lots to see in the area.

reviews.title: A National Treasure
reviews.text: Located on the National Mall, the Lincoln Memorial is one that is a must-see while in the city! The deeply rooted history in the memorial is one both history lovers and everyday spectators will love!

reviews.title: Sightseeing in Washington, D.C.
reviews.text: If you are visiting D.C., you should definitely pay a visit to Lincoln Memorial built to honor the 16th President of the United States, Abraham Lincoln.

reviews.title: Great Day Trip
reviews.text: My aunt and I went here on a Saturday morning. It was not too crowded, slightly touristy, but many people exercising in and enjoying the capitol. The Lincoln Memorial is an amazing experience if you have never seen it before. The architecture and sculpture is beautiful, especially when you see it in person!

reviews.title: Didn't climb the stairs this time but it is a moving memorial
reviews.text: There are a LOT of stairs.  But it is moving to see this memorial and contemplate what it must have been like to be president during the Civil War.  There may be an elevator but when I looked at the crowd, almost no one was wearing a mask and I did not want to expose myself to them.

reviews.title: It is breathtaking

reviews.title: Never enough time to soak it all in

reviews.title: Iconic and breathtaking.

reviews.title: History

reviews.title: A must see monument

reviews.title: Day Trip

reviews.title: Absolutely a Must. Very moving, every single time.

reviews.title: Spectacular

reviews.text: We visited during COVID. It wasn’t real crowded. There were 2 park rangers on site and they were happy to answer our questions. The monument is beautiful with all of the detail and history. Standing inside and looking out over the mall is inspiring and makes you proud of our country.

reviews.text: very nice views from all around the Memorial. I like to visit in late afternoon or early evening when the crowds have decreased. Across the Independence Ave is the Martin Luther King Jr Memorial and along the west side of Tidal Basin is the Franklin Delano Roosevelt Memorial then you will see the Jefferson Memorial.NOTE: If you are calling a ride share car, pick up is on the south side of Lincoln Memorial where the taxis and buses pick up and drop off.

reviews.title: Don’t miss this
reviews.text: We visited this monument in the ‘before times’ - before masks, social distancing and the like. Back then it was quite crowded, but this visit, it was practically deserted. We were able to walk right up and only saw about 20 other people on the monument. Everyone was masked and able to observe social distancing, so it was perfectly comfortable. If you’re in DC, don’t miss this iconic landmark.

reviews.title: What would he be thinking?
reviews.text: The Lincoln memorial was one of the highlights of my visit to the capital. It is a grand tribute to the greatest president in US history. The building is beautiful, it towers over the reflecting pool on the western side of the National Mall. Lincoln himself is embodied in 19ft high stature, weighing in at 175 tons. The Gettysburg address is chiseled in on one side of the building and the second inaugural address on the other. As the nation today stands more divided than ever since the civil war you can’t help wondering what Lincoln is thinking as he is gazing out on the capital from his chair.

reviews.title: Must See

reviews.title: Significant Impact

reviews.title: Lincoln

reviews.title: Moving experience
reviews.text: One of the best places on earth! Sit and reflect, read the words, meditate on them. Take in the views and be in awe of what you as an American are entitled to. This is your city, your monuments!

reviews.title: Honestly, You Should See Abe
reviews.text: If you somehow can't make it to all of the national monuments in DC you should make it a point to see the Lincoln Memorial at the very least. It's impressive on it's own but the reflective pool provides gorgeous scenery and you can see some of the other surrounding monuments from the top of the steps. Going during the day is well and good but it's equally as eye catching at night and provides a quiet and calm atmosphere to soak in the history.

reviews.title: Amazing gentleman who cared about all.
reviews.text: This memorial is the start of an amazing area in our nation's capital that honors what our nation is all about, sacrifice,  honor,  equality, and faith in each other.  Abraham Lincoln's speech on the wall of this memorial says it all.   If no time to read the whole speech then read they final paragraph.... it says it all!  We all need to remember what we are,  why we are, and why this country is great.  One Nation Under God, all equal.

reviews.title: One of the Best
reviews.text: Lots of monuments in DC, but the Lincoln Memorial is probably one of the most moving. It's hard to visualize just how much space the entire grounds occupies.

reviews.title: The 16th President
reviews.text: The memorial seems huge and towering when you're at the bottom of the steps and the steps seem huge as you walk up them; when I visited in 2012 I tried to race up the steps but tripped halfway up, luckily no one else seemed to notice. Once you get tot he top step you can turn around and see the Washington monument in the distance in front of the long lake, for some reason the water was drained that day. At the entrance of the memorial since it blocks out the sun, the statue is shrouded in the shadows so you can't really see it until you enter. Once you go inside, your eyes adjust to the dark, and then you see him, a huge statue but with a gentle face staring out at Washington. On the walls beside him are quotes from some of his famous speeches like the Gettysburg address and the sight has even more historical significance when you remember that MLK's I have a dream speech was held here decades ago. This memorial gives you a link to America's history, it's both majestic and educational.

reviews.title: STATELY MONUMENT
reviews.text: It is impressive and it is the most visited site. It is an iconic monument, which is worth a view. We really had fantastic photos on the steps of the Lincoln Memorial. It was my second visit but accompanied with my husband and our older daughter, which was their first time.

reviews.title: Impressive monument
reviews.text: We visited Lincoln memorial on our trip to US with SOTC group. The building is very impressive and is a beautiful monument in Washington DC. There is a huge statue of Abraham Lincoln inside the hall. The place was bit crowded and had to wait for our turn to take pictures. There is a pool in front of the building and the memorial is facing Capitol Building. On a bright sunny day, you can take great pictures from the top of the steps of the building. A must see in washingtom

reviews.title: fitting tribute
reviews.text: Gargantuan memorial to one of our best leaders. As a native Illinoisan, it was nice to see it. 2013 visit.

reviews.title: A Moving, Must-See Memorial
reviews.text: My son and  visited the Lincoln Memorial on our recent trip to DC.  The Memorial is one of the signature monuments in DC.  It is a beautiful monument and grand in scale.  It sits at the opposite end of the National Mall from the US Capitol Building.  The memorial contains a very large statue of Abraham Lincoln seated in the center of the monument.  The statue is posed to reflect the two sides of Lincoln, the firm Lincoln who vowed to stop the Southern States from secession and the conciliatory and the kind Lincoln who wanted to welcome the Southern Stars back as brothers at the end of the Civil War. It is a very moving monument.  Also the views from the top of the steps are terrific.  You can see the reflecting pool and the Washington Monument and the Capitol Building and more.  This is a must see in Washington.

reviews.title: Quite impressive
reviews.text: This Monument is quite impressive. We were quite lucky and it was pretty quiet so we managed to get some good photos. The pond in front had no water so that was a bit disappointing but we had a sunny day so it was lovely taking a moment on the stairs and admiring the views. Lincoln's statue is so impressive - much bigger than I thought it would be. Loved reading about the history of it in the museum underneath. Definitely worth a visit.

reviews.title: Love this area - so interesting.
reviews.text: We spent a huge day in the Capitol area and walked a long way enjoying the buildings. So impressive, all in their own way. We were sorry to only have a short time and would recommend spending a long weekend in DC to make the most of these fabulous buildings.

reviews.title: Night visit
reviews.text: Took a small evening "golf cart" type tour here. The lighting was perfect and made for great photos and less crowds.

reviews.title: One of those things you must have visited

reviews.title: Lincoln Memorial
reviews.text: This was much small than I always thought it was. Lots of people inside made it hard to walk around and see.

reviews.title: Historic
reviews.text: I loved the Lincoln Memorial and all the stories that go a long with it. I was on an African American History tour, so we heard stories from the architecture of the building, the meaning behind the words around the inside of the memorial, to the significance behind delivering the momentous I Have A Dream Speech at such an important location. I would’ve loved to see this monument at night which they say is a beautiful sight.

reviews.title: Spend time reading speeches.  Don't miss where MLK stood

reviews.text: Of course you know this is a must-see! It can be busy during the day and President Lincoln is in a half enclosed area so maybe go in the morning or evening for thinner crowds.

reviews.title: Beautiful and awe inspiring!
reviews.text: The Lincoln monument is an absolute must visit. Honestly there is something unique and special about each monument but the view of the Lincoln monument at night is priceless. Take a minute and snap a picture of your loved ones along pillars on the sides with the Washington monument in the background. Perfect backdrop, magnificent setting and a truly special monument!

reviews.title: Impressive Monument
reviews.text: I have been to DC several times and have seen the Lincoln Memorial more than once. It is quite impressive. This trip I viewed the monument in the evening...awesome. It is really quite majestic all lit up. The monument is a wealth of history and standing where MLK gave his “I have a Dream” speech is empowering.

reviews.title: Tour by bicycle

reviews.title: So much history

reviews.title: Breathtaking!

reviews.title: Great historic monument.
reviews.text: We visited the memorial whilst on a tour so received a lot of facts and information about Lincoln, the Civil War, the Gettysburg Address, etc.  It's a very impressive, huge memorial, but what makes it extra special is the Martin Luther King step just outside the memorial, from which he made the iconic "I have a Dream" speech.  It lead us to researching a lot about Americal History when we returned to the UK.

reviews.title: Breathtaking Experience

reviews.title: A must see

reviews.title: Absolutely Must Visit
reviews.text: The view from the top of the steps looking across the reflecting pool one half mile (or more) to the Washington Monument is beyond breathtaking. The soft kindness in the face of the President contrasts with the massive angular granite from which it is carved. I am not a big souvenir guy but I just had to buy something from the gift shop to take a piece of this experience home with me.

reviews.title: Worth the trek up those stairs!

The TV also makes this seem like a quick walk, but it's not. It's a beautiful stroll from one end to the other.

Take some time to read the walls and take some pictures, then sit on the front steps for a while and take it all in.  10 years from now, this is the memorial I will remember.

reviews.title: Amazing in person.

reviews.title: So serene and vast and stunning

The stillness of the water against all the surrounding memorials and waving American flags is just so beautiful and peaceful. Washington is one of the nicest cities I have ever been to. Absolutely loved the Lincoln Memorial, it's stunning and so well looked after. Well done America, it's a masterpiece.

reviews.title: Lincoln Memorial

If you are unable to climb those stairs, you can take the old elevator up to the chamber and see Lincoln himself! It is also nice to just sit on the ledge on the back of the monument and plane watch! Definetly recommend!

reviews.title: Must see in DC

Of course the view from anywhere around the monument is amazing, but my favorite is sitting on the steps looking towards the Capitol.

reviews.title: Great at night and has bathrooms!
reviews.text: Nothing compares with the view from the top steps of the Lincoln Memorial.  Truly inspiring.  The monument is open all night (or at least until really late) so it's a great place to explore at after dark.  And a little know fact is that there are indoor bathrooms in the basement along with a small museum.

reviews.title: Washington's Parthenon
reviews.text: The Lincoln memorial very much has the appearance of a colonnaded temple and also has the vast feeling of a cathedral. Our visit during the day was very busy and it was difficult to appreciate the architecture and the fact that it is a memorial. We returned during the evening where we able to enjoy this enduring symbol in spectacular lighting, definitely a better time to view if you can.

reviews.title: Check out the exhibit downstairs!!
reviews.text: The Lincoln Memorial is by far one of the most amazing things about DC. It will always be a "must see" of any trip. What we didn't know about was the cool little exhibit downstairs by the restrooms. It's very small, but really neat! It's mainly photos of the competition to see what the design would be and different events that have taken place there over the years.  It will only take about 10 mins to walk through, but was a nice little bonus!

reviews.title: The busiest memorial

The amount of different languages heard on the steps is a tribute to the impact this man had, not only in the United States, but a reputation that goes worldwide. Truly impactful . 4th visit in my lifetime.    Little known fact, the Memorial and Washington Monument are perfectly aligned to block the Capital building.

reviews.title: The Must See
reviews.text: The history behind Lincoln Memorial is inspiring, the father of the American union receives his recognition in an awe-inspiring moment in the heart of DC. The Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. “I have a dream” speech monument, in the center of the stairs is really nice and represents the struggle of millions.

reviews.title: Lincoln Memorial

If you come here in. the morning after a fresh snowfall, it's magical. I try to avoid the place when there are lots of tourists.
